_comment: The poisoning corpus (plans/os-e2f1ad23.md D1, D2): one scripted trajectory per name, each ending in an attempt to promote a false lesson, each asserted to fail at both ends. gate names a registered curation gate (curation.Gates()); a poison the boundary refuses outside the registry names its reason instead. Every registered gate has at least one poison, derived and pinned by internal/admit/poisoning_test.go.

poisons.name: deadend-bare-pointer
poisons.attack: the holder records a dead end whose pointer is a bare path, so the observation cites a file no reader can resolve at a commit

poisons.name: deadend-not-holder
poisons.attack: a second worker records a dead end inside the holder's window, planting an observation on a trajectory it never worked

poisons.name: proposal-smuggled-field
poisons.attack: the curator's proposal carries an extra key (a lesson path), hoping a reader treats the proposal as already promoted

poisons.name: subject-forged
poisons.attack: the curator proposes on a subject not derived from the claim, so a second proposal of the same claim could stand beside it

poisons.name: predicate-everything
poisons.attack: an empty applies-when, so the lesson would surface on every claim in the deployment

poisons.name: predicate-unknown-field
poisons.attack: an applies-when naming a field the record does not derive, so no claim could be shown to fall outside it

poisons.name: unchanged-reproposal
poisons.attack: a contested claim re-proposed with the same claim and the same exceptions, hoping the contest does not follow it

poisons.name: forged-support
poisons.attack: support citing a position that is no observation, a raise carrying a finding, and a position beyond the tip

poisons.name: grantless-window
poisons.attack: a grantless key raw-pushes a claim on a ready contract and a dead end inside the apparent window, then the curator cites it

poisons.name: failed-support
poisons.attack: support citing a contract whose authentic verdict is a fail, after the implementer raw-pushed a pass over it

poisons.name: single-success
poisons.attack: one contract, two dead ends: a single run dressed as two observations

poisons.name: self-replay
poisons.attack: two contracts held by one key, in a family with two holders: one worker replaying its own trajectory as independent support

poisons.name: contest-smuggled-field
poisons.attack: a contest carrying an extra key, hoping a reader takes it for a promotion or an exception

poisons.name: contest-phantom
poisons.attack: a contest citing a position that is no admitted hypothesis, so the contested stage could be planted on a subject nobody proposed

poisons.name: contest-forged-evidence
poisons.attack: a contest whose evidence is a raise carrying a finding: a question dressed as a counter-observation

poisons.name: contest-unselected
poisons.attack: a contest whose evidence lies on a contract the applies-when never selected, so the claim was never supposed to hold there

poisons.name: held-out-forgery
poisons.attack: a contest citing the support set itself as counter-evidence

poisons.name: promotion-traversal
poisons.attack: a promotion whose lesson path climbs out of the store through .., naming a file the store's lint never sees

poisons.name: promotion-of-raw-proposal
poisons.attack: a promotion citing a well-shaped proposal a claim key raw-pushed past the boundary

poisons.name: contested-promotion
poisons.attack: a promotion of a hypothesis a contest already stands against

poisons.name: unknown-carrier
poisons.attack: a promotion naming a carrier outside the member set (a prompt), so no rule would know where the lesson lands

poisons.name: stamps-unordered
poisons.attack: a promotion whose expiry precedes its last validation, so the lesson would never be due for revalidation

poisons.name: digest-malformed
poisons.attack: a promotion whose digest is not a sha256, so no reader could verify the file it names

poisons.name: smuggled-role-lesson
poisons.attack: a role carrier promoted citing a pass on an ordinary contract that carries no eval marker

poisons.name: raw-pass
poisons.attack: a pass a key raw-pushed before it was granted verdict, cited as the adversarial evaluation

poisons.name: borrowed-pass
poisons.attack: a pass on an eval whose marker binds another hypothesis, and one bound to another carrier revision

poisons.name: stale-pass
poisons.attack: a pass on an eval filed before the hypothesis existed: a counter-trajectory constructed against nothing

poisons.name: fail-as-survival
poisons.attack: a fail verdict cited as the adversarial evaluation

poisons.name: support-failed-later
poisons.attack: a hypothesis admitted over a trajectory that fails afterwards, promoted as if its support still stood

poisons.name: frontmatter-missing
poisons.attack: a lesson file with no frontmatter block, so nothing binds it to a hypothesis

poisons.name: frontmatter-drift
poisons.attack: a lesson file citing another hypothesis than the fact that promoted it

poisons.name: predicate-drift
poisons.attack: a lesson file whose applies-when is wider than the hypothesis's, so the file would be read on claims the boundary never admitted it for

poisons.name: support-drift
poisons.attack: a lesson file listing support the hypothesis never cited

poisons.name: fabricated-provenance
poisons.attack: a provenance anchor the repository lacks at its commit

poisons.name: digest-drift
poisons.attack: a fact whose digest is not the bytes of the file at its anchor: the file was rewritten after the promotion

poisons.name: unmerged-anchor
poisons.attack: an anchor commit that exists on a branch and is no ancestor of the head: the promotion PR never merged

poisons.name: stamps-future
poisons.attack: a last-validated stamp in the future, so the lesson reads as freshly validated forever

poisons.name: carrier-drift
poisons.attack: a lesson file naming another carrier than the fact, so the file lands where the boundary never judged it

poisons.name: worker-proposes
poisons.attack: a claim key proposes over its own admitted observations

poisons.name: root-proposes
poisons.attack: a governance root, holding operator implicitly, proposes: the fifth no-fallback row

poisons.name: worker-granted-curate
poisons.attack: the operator grants curate to a claim key, so one key could observe and propose

poisons.name: ungated-eval
poisons.attack: an executable eval specified without gate evidence, so an unreviewed counter-trajectory could be the adversarial evaluation

poisons.name: raw-pushed-promotion
poisons.attack: a promotion the adversarial gate refused, pushed past the boundary: the fold re-judges it at its position, binds nothing, and no claim receives it

poisons.name: raw-pushed-contest
poisons.attack: a contest the held-out gate refused, pushed past the boundary to disable a legitimate lesson: the fold re-judges it at its position and the lesson keeps surfacing

poisons.name: pass-at-another-position
poisons.attack: the survived eval's submission position cited as its verdict: a pass exists on the chain, at another position

poisons.name: contested-surfacing
poisons.attack: a promoted lesson re-promoted after its contest, hoping the delivery reads the promotion rather than the stage

poisons.name: stamps-unreviewed
poisons.attack: a promotion recording lifecycle dates the lesson PR never reviewed: the fact's expires is later than the frontmatter's, so the lesson would outlive its review

poisons.name: re-promotion-stale-stamps
poisons.attack: a re-promotion of the same path at a new anchor with a fresh adversarial pass and the old last_validated stamp, so the file changes without anyone revalidating it

poisons.name: retirement-smuggled-field
poisons.attack: a retirement carrying an extra key (a rewritten lesson body), hoping a reader takes the retirement as an edit of the evidence

poisons.name: regression-without-revert
poisons.attack: a regression retirement without the revert's pr, a pr riding the expired reason, and a reason the contract does not name: each takes the promotion out without the evidence its reason requires

poisons.name: retire-superseded-promotion
poisons.attack: a retirement citing the earlier promotion of a path after a revalidation superseded it, so the path reads retired while its latest promotion stands

poisons.name: superseded-by-itself
poisons.attack: a superseded retirement whose superseded_by names the retired promotion itself, an earlier position, or a position that is no promotion, so the conclusion is revoked with nothing standing in its place

poisons.name: deadend-retire-cross-contract
poisons.attack: a dead-end retirement on one contract citing another contract's dead end, so a curator retires evidence on a trajectory the act is not a fact on

poisons.name: deadend-retire-phantom
poisons.attack: a dead-end retirement citing a park, not a dead end, so the act flags an observation that was never a dead end

poisons.name: deadend-retire-same-environment
poisons.attack: a dead-end retirement naming the environment the dead end was recorded in, so the dead end is flagged while it still applies

poisons.name: unretire-without-retirement
poisons.attack: an un-retirement of a dead end nobody retired, planting a standing act that a later retirement would then have to un-do

poisons.name: duplicate-lesson
poisons.attack: a second lesson file citing the hypothesis a file already carries, so the store holds two conclusions for one claim

poisons.name: frontmatter-smuggled-key
poisons.attack: a frontmatter key the contract does not name (a stage), a body missing its evidence section, and the sections out of order: each reads as a lesson while carrying something the README never asked for
